sections.title: Cystitis
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z SOME DRUGS THAT CAUSE AND CURE CYSTITIS WITH INDICATIONS. Aco. * Apis * Arn. * Bell. * Canth. * Caust. * Cham. * Chim. * Dulc. * Equis. * Lach. * Lyc. * Merc. cor. * Par. b. * Petr. * Puls. * Sars. * Sep. * Staph. * Tarent. h. * Tereb. [ Top ] CANTHARIS The remedy par excellence of cystitis. Violent tenesmus and strangury ( Lil. tigr. ). Painful discharge of a few drops of bloody urine with very severe pain, as if a red-hot iron were passed along urethra. Violent burning, cutting, stabbing pain in neck of bladder. - worse before and after urinating. Urging to urinate, from smallest quantity urine in bladder ( Puls. ). Must double up and scream from the pain. Urine only drop by drop ( Apis ) with extreme pain. "Cures acute cystitis more frequently than all other remedies put together." - (FARRINGTON.) GUERNSEY : " It is a singular fact, that if there be frequent micturition attended with burning, cutting pain, or if burning and cutting attend the flow, Canth. is almost always the remedy for whatever other suffering there may be, even in inflammation of brain or lungs ." KENT : "The most important feature of this medicine is the rapidity with which it develops a gangrenous state... The patient is violently sick in a great hurry... The bladder and genitals are inflamed, and the excitement and congestion often arouse the sexual instinct to sexual thoughts, and even sexual frenzy... Intensity and rapidity are its features. A state of pain and excitement found in no other remedy." [ Top ] TARENTULA H. Cystitis with high fever, gastric derangement ; excruciating pains and impossibility to pass a drop of urine. Bladder seems swollen and hard. Great spasmodic tenesmus. Passes by drops a dark-red, brown, fetid urine, with gravel-like sediment. Excessive restlessness : hurried and fidgety : rolls from side to side. [ Top ] PAREIRA BRAVA Atrocious pains with strangury. Constant urging : violent pain extorts screams. Must get down on hand and knees to urinate : almost touches floor with forehead, in order to be able to pass urine. (Comp. Chimaph ., Sarsa. ). Pains down thighs in efforts to urinate. Passes stringy white mucus, or red sand. [ Top ] APIS Excessive pain in region of bladder. Frequent, painful, scanty, bloody urination. Much straining, then a few drops : dribbles a little hot bloody urine ( Canth. ). Urine almost suppressed. Scanty urine in little boys, with foreskin enormously distended, or hydrocele. When call comes to urinate, will shriek, because he remembers the pain last time ( Acon. ). Whole urinary tract irritated, like Canth. : - " these two, antidote one another ." Agony in voiding urine. Retention in nursing infants. KENT says : "Old women knew, long before Apis was proved, that when the new-born babe did not pass its water, they could find a cure by catching bees, over which they poured hot water, and gave the baby a teaspoonful." The pains of Apis are burning, stinging . Apis is worse from heat : better from cold . Has plenty of dema. Is thirstless (Rev. of Acon. ). [ Top ] BELLADONNA No remedy has a greater irritation of bladder and along urinary tract. Urging to urinate constant. Urine dribbles : burns intensely along length of urethra. Bladder sensitive to pressure : to jar. After urination sits and strains : intense torment. Sometimes bloody urination : or blood in bladder comes away in little clots. Urine strongly acid. Fiery red urine. Bell. has quick sensations and motion. Pains come suddenly, and go suddenly. Bell. in fever, craves lemons. Is usually hot, and red. Tends to violent delirium. [ Top ] ACONITE Inflammation of bladder and kidneys ; bloody urine. Violent burning in bladder. Urine scanty, suppressed or retained. From shock . Cystitis ; cutting, tearing pains : burning. Urine hot, dark, red ; clear or bloody. Retention from cold. In children urging ; crying ; fear of the pain ( Apis ). "Inflammation of bladder, in adults or infants : with the Aconite anxiety ; restlessness ; fear." - KENT. Acon. is thirsty : Apis thirstless. [ Top ] SARSAPARILLA Unbearable pain at end of urination ( Equiset .). Tenderness and distension of bladder. Cannot pass urine when sitting : it passes freely when standing. Dribbles while sitting. Floods the bed at night ; by day can only pass it standing. "Passes enormous quantities of sand. In one case, this mitigated the catarrh and kept bladder comfortable." - KENT. Also, "Urine passed without sensation." (See Caust. ) [ Top ] TEREBINTH Violent burning and cutting in bladder, alternating with similar pain in umbilicus < at rest , > walking in open air . (Comp. Puls. ). Sensitive in hypogastrium ; tenesmus, bladder. Spasmodic tenesmus, urging and pressing while sitting : pain streaks up to kidneys. Hæmaturia : albuminuria : urine cloudy, smoky . (A great hæmorrhagic remedy). Smooth, glossy, red tongue ( Pyrog. , Crot. ). Urine smells strongly of violets. Tereb. has also excessive tympanites. Ecchymoses : purpura (A less acute Canth. ). [ Top ] EQUISETUM Dull pain in bladder, as from distension. Constant desire to urinate and pass large quantities of pale urine without relief. HERING'S case : - "General paralysis in an old woman in whom control over stools and urine, long completely lost, was rapidly restored." Has severe pain at end of urination ( Sarsa. ). [ Top ] LACHESIS Cystitis with offensive mucus, tending to putrescence. "The more the offensiveness, the more it is Lach. " Sensitiveness over abdomen. Can hardly allow her clothes to touch her. Urine blackish, or dark brown : foamy : or has little black spots like soot floating in it. Feeling as of a ball rolling about in bladder or abdomen. Ineffectual urging ; Violent burning when it does pass. No urine : no stool. Always has to urinate after lying down : especially after sleep. Typically Lach. is purple : loquacious : suspicious : sleeps into an aggravation, or is worse after sleep. Is hypersensitive to heat and touch. [ Top ] CHIMAPHILA UMBELLATA Cystitis with great quantities of ropy bloody mucus in urine : muco-purulent : foul, scanty. Curious sensation of swelling in perineum, or near anus, "as if sitting on a ball." Must stand, feet wide apart to urinate. (Comp. Sarsa. ). "Prostatic troubles" - NASH. Acute inflammation in urinary tract. [ Top ] PULSATILLA Wonderful tenesmus : extremely painful, bloody, burning, smarting urine : scarcely a drop collects in bladder, but it must be expelled ( Canth. ). Cannot lie on back, without desire to urinate. Dribbling urine : on slightest provocation - coughing, sneezing, (Comp. Caust. ), surprise, joy, laughing, the slam of a door ( Sep. ). Great urgency : impossible to delay : when going to urinate, sensation as if it will gush away. Tenesmus vesicæ : cystitis or catarrh. As if bladder too full. Must keep mind constantly on bladder, or she will lose her urine ( Sepia ). Flows away in sleep ( Lyc. , Caust. , etc.). In the Pulsatilla patient : changeable, extremely touchy and weepy. Heat and stuffiness unbearable. (Comp. Terebinth. ). [ Top ] CHAMOMILLA Sticking pain in neck of bladder when not urinating : burning pain, when urinating. Ineffectual urging, with anguish : smarting or burning in urethra when urinating. Urine hot, scanty, turbid ; red as blood. But with the Cham. mentality :- Piteous moaning, in child : because he cannot have what he wants. Wants this and that, then pushes it away. Snappish : uncivil : irritable : impatient. Oversensitive to pain : "cannot bear it." [ Top ] STAPHISAGRIA KENT says, " Staphysagria is very comforting to the young wife." Frequent and painful urging to urinate : urine bloody, involuntary, acrid and corroding, with burning : worse from motion. Burning during and after urination. NASH says, "our only remedy for burning all the time, between the acts of urinating." A remedy of strong mentality : ailments from indignation about acts of others - or his own. [ Top ] ARNICA Bladder affections after mechanical injuries. Constant urging, while urine passes involuntarily by drops. Frequent attempts to urinate : has to wait a long time for urine to pass. Urination involuntarily during sleep : when running. Hæmaturia from mechanical causes : Urine thick, with much pus. Urine very acrid, with increased specific gravity. With Arn. the body feels sore and bruised, and the bed too hard. Fear of touch : of approach. A curious symptom : says she is well, when very ill. [ Top ] PETROSELINUM Such pain when he passes urine, as to cause him to shiver and dance round the room in agony. Sudden agonizing desire to urinate. [ Top ] MERCURIUS COR. Tenesmus vesicæ with intense burning in urethra ; discharge of mucus and blood with urine or after it. Micturition frequent : urine in drops with much pain. Scanty : hot ; burning ; bloody ( Canth. , Apis ). Stools also hot, scanty, bloody, with great straining, not relieved by stool. (Dysentery). Ptyalism, with salty taste. Skin cold, pale, dripping with sweat. A remedy of violent conditions. [ Top ] DULCAMARA Cystitis, or catarrh of bladder : from changes in the weather : from hot to cold : especially to damp cold. If chilled must hurry to urinate. "Every time he takes a little cold, urine bloody, with frequency." - KENT. Constant desire to urinate, felt deep in abdomen. Dulc. is a medicine of Autumn ; hot days and cold evenings. They bring out sweat, then suppress it. " Dulc. is for affections of damp cold , what Acon. is for the same, from dry cold ." - NASH. [ Top ] CAUSTICUM Frequent urging, day and night. Ineffectual attempts to urinate : when a few drops passed, had violent pain in bladder. Urging : had to wait a long time, when only a little passed : urging soon renewed without pain. Painful retention, brought on by cold ( Acon. ). Catarrh of bladder. Queer symptom, itching at urethral orifice. KENT says, Caust. has two kinds of paralysis of bladder : one of muscles of expulsion, when urine is retained : one sphincter vesicæ, when urine is passed involuntarily. Again, paralysis of bladder, from over-distension ; after having to delay urination. Post-operative retention. [ Top ] SEPIA Sepia also, may be compelled to keep her mind on the neck of the bladder, or she will lose her urine ( Puls. ). Enuresis when coughing, laughing, the slam of a door, or when mind is diverted ( Puls. ). Constant urging for a milky urine that burns like fire, and deposits a material hard to wash off the vessel. Bloody urine, scanty and suppressed : sudden desire, and tenesmus as if uterus would come out . "Sudden desire with cutting like knives, and chill all over the body." - KENT. More chronic, and in the Sepia patient. Indifferent : cold, mentally : no joy in life. Chilly ; sallow : brownish skin. Faint sinking at epigastrium. Wants to get away and be at peace. (Antithesis of Puls. ). [ Top ] LYCOPODIUM Cystitis : turbid, milky urine, with offensive purulent sediment : dull pressing in bladder and abdomen. Heaviness in bladder. Urging to urinate : must wait long before it will pass, with constant bearing down. Supports abdomen with hands. (Vulva, Sep. ). Urging, children cry out and grasp abdomen. "Copious red sand in urine, in acute cases : in chronic, when the patient feels best, red sand is found in urine." - KENT. Involuntary urination in sleep. Polyuria during the night, though normal or even scanty by day. Involuntary in sleep. Passes enormous quantities of urine, very clear and of light specific gravity. Red sand in the baby's diaper : the urine causes great irritation where left in contact with skin. But in the Lyc. patient ; more mental than physical development. Worse 4-8 P. M. Desire for sweets and hot drinks. A remedy of great flatulence and fullness after eating but a little. [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Deafness
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z SOME REMEDIES OF DEAFNESS WITH INDICATIONS. Agraph. n. * Amb. * Arn. * Bar. c. * Bar. m. * Bell. * Calc. * Carb. an. * Caust. * Chen. an. * Graph. * Hep. * Hyos. * Kali m. * Luet. * Lyc. * Med. * Morb. * Nat. m. * Nit. ac. * Parot. * Phos. * Pneum. * Puls. * Spig. * Strep. * Sulph. MANY different causes may be responsible for "deafness" (including WAX ). We will try to give some of its most useful remedies with indications for their use. [ Top ] BELLADONNA Sensation of a skin drawn over the ears. Acute inflammation of ear, with screaming delirium rolling of head : threatened meningitis. [ Top ] CALCAREA Perversions of hearing. As if something lay in front of membrana tympani. Hardness of hearing, especially after suppression of intermittents by quinine ( Nat. mur. ) also from Eustachian catarrh. Deafness, right-sided : worse open air : better from sweating. Dryness in ears ( Graph .), or purulent discharge. Polypus in ears ( Lyc ., ? Morbillinum ). With inflammation of parotid. Calcarea is chilly : perspiring : especially : head and neck at night : typically fat and indolent. (The Chronic of Belladonna .) [ Top ] CAUSTICUM Deafness, as if ears closed. Loud reverberations of sound ; of one's owe words in the ear ( Phos .). CAUST. typically, is weak and emaciated : ha weakness, to paralysis, of parts as, drooping ; eyelids, incontinence of urine. Melancholy and weeping : "the least thin makes the child cry." [ Top ] PHOSPHORUS Deafness with cold extremities. Difficult of hearing the human voice : with loud reverberation of words in ears ( Caust .) ; extending into head. Typical Phos . is worse in the dark : when alone : in a thunder-storm. Has burning everywhere, mouth, stomach, spine, palm etc. Craves cold things, ice-cream, salt. Thirst for cold water. An easy bleeder of bright blood. "A remedy of great range and great power." [ Top ] SPIGELIA Periodic deafness : ears feel stuffed. When speaking, one's voice resounds like a bell through brain. (Comp. Caust ., Phos ., Sulph .) Neuralgia of ears. A great nerve and headache medicine : worse touch ; motion ; jar ; with the sun. [ Top ] LYCOPODIUM Impairment or loss of hearing in connection with otorrha. Loss of hearing : loss of speech, because unable to hear words. Small ulcers or polypi in ear ( Calc ., ? Morbillinum ). But in the Lycopodium patient : better mental than physical development. Worse warmth ; better cold, yet wants hot drinks. Indigestion with excessive flatulence and distension. Worse pressure of clothes. [ Top ] SULPHUR Deafness, preceded by over-sensitiveness of hearing ; especially for human voice : worse after eating, or blowing nose. Curious sensation, as if sounds did not come through ears, but through forehead and brain. (Comp. Spig .) Deafness after acute illness, in a Sulphur patient : hot : hungry : untidy : with a love of fats, and relief from uncovering. [ Top ] PULSATILLA One of our greatest ear remedies-in a Puls . patient. i. e. Intolerant of heat : of close rooms : of fat and indigestible food. Weepy and querulous. After suppressed measles, with otorrha. [ Top ] HEPAR Also in black type for deafness. Discharge of fetid pus from ears. Canal filled with white, cheesy, bloody pus little pustules in meatus and auricle where ever pus touched ; hæmorrhage from slightest touch. > hot applications : cannot bear anything cold. Hepar is hypersensitive physically and mentally. Worse cold ; uncovering ; touch. Better warm wraps ; damp weather ( Medorrh .). [ Top ] KALI MURIATICUM "Deafness : from swelling of internal ear from swelling of Eustachian tubes and tympanitic cavity : with swelling of glands, or cracking noise on blowing nose, or white coated tongue." Kali muriaticum is easily intoxicated by wine or beer. Has marked increase in dandruff : with itching. "Of use in second stage of inflammation, or stage of interstitial exudation, in any part of body : - a remedy of great value. " - NASH. [ Top ] AGRAPHIS NUTANS Throat deafness : adenoids : enlarged tonsils. Throat and ear troubles with free discharge from mucous membranes. Takes cold easily from exposure to cold winds. [ Top ] AMBRA Deafness of one ear, noises in the other. Increasing deafness : with cold sensation in abdomen. Ambra is worn out, yet over-impressionable. Is much affected by music. Cannot pass stool, or urine ( Nat. mur. ) in presence of others. Discharge of blood between periods, from slight exertion. [ Top ] BARYTA MUR. Deaf : with vomiting ; headache ; burning in stomach and convulsions. Otorrha : discharge from ears smelling like rotten cheese. Parotids swollen, hard. Baryta carb ., "only more so." [ Top ] BARYTA CARB. Difficult hearing. Big tonsils. Quinsy (cm. potency), recurrent quinsy. Typical Baryta carb . is dwarfish, mind and body. Hair falls off : baldness. Baryta carb . is distrustful, shy. Very sensitive to cold. [ Top ] HYOSCYAMUS One dose of the strong tincture amazingly restored hearing for some hours, in a case of nerve deafness. Should be helpful-perhaps only after the basic cause has been dealt with. DEAFNESS . Hardness of hearing from paralysed auditory nerves. Hard hearing, as if stupified, especially after apoplexy. [ Top ] CHENOPODIUM ANTHELMINTICUM Torpor of auditory nerve. Hearing better for high-pitched sounds. Comparative deafness to sound of voice, painfully sensitive to sound, as of passing vehicles. Shrinks from low tones. Aural vertigo. "Progressive deafness to human voice, extreme sensitiveness to other sounds (cerebral deafness).'' - CLARKE. [ Top ] ARNICA Hard hearing from concussions. In affections in general the results of trauma. Has cured deafness after typhus, measles with swelling of parotid gland, etc. Typical indications :-bruised sore feeling all over : bed too hard. Ecchymoses, spontaneous or from injury. Recent and remote affections from injuries. Hæmorrhages from mechanical injuries. [ Top ] GRAPHITES Deafness with dry external meatus. With watery discharge from ears ; mucous membrane red and excoriated : eczematous rash on face : tympani not perforated, but appear covered with a white coating. Hears better when in a noise. A characteristic symptom is, moist eruption behind ears. A great skin medicine : with lumpy hard skin, cracks, fissures : irritable, dry skin, or eruptions that exude a gluey moisture. Supersensitive to cold. Apprehensive, inclined to weep. Sensitive to music. One of the medicines of obesity ( Calc .). [ Top ] CARBO AN. Hearing weak and confused : tones become commingled : he cannot tell from which side they come, and it seems as though they came from another world. Ichorous otorrha. Parotid gland swollen and indurated. Carbo animalis affects venules. Has blue skin, lips, affected parts. Relief while eating. [ Top ] NITRIC ACID Deafness, better riding in carriage or train. From induration and swelling of tonsils. Eustachian tubes obstructed : throbbing in ears. Otorrha fetid, ichorous ; purulent. Auditory canal nearly closed. Caries mastoid processes. Auditory derangement from swelling of tonsils. Nit. a. has desire for salt and fats, is brown eyed ; chilly ; hates fuss. [ Top ] NATRUM MUR. Hardness of hearing. Deafness from swelling of tympanitic cavity with watery condition of tongue. Catarrh of tympanitic cavity and Eustachian tubes : non-suppurating. Chronic catarrhal otitis with acrid discharge, especially after malaria and much quinine. Nat. mur . hates fuss ; weeps, but no one must see : craves salt ; loathes fat. * * * * * We have purposely omitted "Noises in the Ear", as they are common to all affections of the ear, and have not helped us practically in the effort to discover the vital stimulus of the patient, without which no deep or permanent work can be done. Besides, one argues that, in the same way that anything that impinges on the retina, even to a jar, is translated as light-"I saw stars", -so everything that affects the auditory nerve will be recorded as some kind of sound... as wax, fullness of vessels, pulsation of vessels, thickening of vessels or probably other tissues. They appear to us to be quite outside the question of the treatment of deafness ; though they may, and do, accompany it. [ Top ] MEDORRHINUM Partial or transient deafness : pulsation, ears. Nearly total deafness with very little noise. Sensation of deafness from one ear to the other as if a tube went through head : yet with an over acuteness of hearing. When whistling, sound in ears was double ; with peculiar vibration as when two people whistle thirds. Noises as if in mastoid cells, frying and whistling. Especially in persons with gonorrhal symptoms or history. [ Top ] LUETICUM Deafness, gradually increasing till could scarcely hear at all. Complete deafness, nothing abnormal to be seen. Prescribe on history, or symptoms. [ Top ] STREPTOCOCCIN Has had a marvellous effect on some cases of nerve deafness. Indication, old streptococcic infections. A history of tonsilitis or rheumatism. * * * * * Among the nosodes that might possibly be useful in deafness, the following suggest themselves. We give them tentatively. Apart from the question of loss, or partial loss of hearing, they should improve the health of the patient, "never really well since this, or that acute disease-apparently recovered from." Among these one would mention [ Top ] MORBILLINUM The virus of measles. Ear troubles often follow on measles. It should be one that may help. [ Top ] PNEUMOCOCCIN A homopathic preparation from pneumonia one puts this in, remembering how one patient came into Hospital with pneumonia, stone deaf, and regained his hearing completely as he recovered. [ Top ] PAROTIDINUM A really wonderful preparation where one suspects "the dregs" of mumps to be the basic malady in one or other diseases. Some of the foregoing remedies are said to be useful in deafness "after mumps". [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z SOME REMEDIES OF DENTITION. Aco. * Bell. * Calc. * Calc. ph. * Cham. * Coff. * Kreos. * Podo. * Sulph. * Zinc. [ Top ] CALCAREA Fat, fair, flabby, perspiring. Fontanelles remain open ( Calc. Phos ., Sil. ). Deformed extremities. Deficient, or irregular bone development. Profuse perspiration : soaks the pillow ( Sil. ). Sour sweat : sour diarrha : sour vomit. Flabby ; FAT : lax muscles ; bones that bend. Can't learn to walk ; won't put feet to ground. Milk crust and eruptions in the Calcarea child. Teething cough or diarrha : in the Calcarea child. [ Top ] CALCAREA PHOS. Slow dentition with emaciation (Reverse of Calc. carb. ). Fontanelles remain open. Soft thin skull, crackles when pressed upon. Can't hold head up : it must be supported. Flabby, emaciated : doesn't learn to walk. "Great desire to nurse all the time." Cough with rattling chest. The Calc. phos. child is more wiry ; less fair ; without the sweating head of Calc. Diarrha, stools green and spluttering. Child shrunken and anæmic ( Sil. ). [ Top ] CHAMOMILLA Painful dentition. Oversensitive to pain, which maddens. Very irritable : snaps and snarls ( Cina ). Excessive uneasiness, anxiety, tossing, ( Acon. ). Only to be quieted by being carried about. Drowsiness with sleeplessness. Sweats with the pain. One cheek red and hot, the other pale and cold. Wants this or that, only to push it away. Turmoil in temper, Chamomilla is frantic : "cannot bear it !" Dentition diarrha ( Calc. , Kreos. ). Stools green : odour like rotten eggs : colicky pain. Draws the legs up. Abdomen bloated. [ Top ] KREOSOTUM "Child suffering from very painful dentition : won't sleep at night unless caressed and fondled all the time." ( Cham , unless carried up and down the room). Gums painful, dark-red or blue : teeth decay as soon as they come. May have constipation, or diarrha. Cholera infantum during teething : very severe : vomiting incessant, with cadaveric-smelling stools. [ Top ] ACONITE Feverish. Fever. Dry hot skin ( Bell. ). Child gnaws its fists ; frets and cries. Sleepless ; excited ; tosses ; heat ; startings and twitchings ( Bell. ) Of single muscles. Convulsions of teething children ( Bell. ). Costive, or dark, watery stools. [ Top ] COFFEA Wakeful : constantly on the move. Not distressed : happy, but sleepless. Remarkable wakefulness. Over excitement of brain. [ Top ] BELLADONNA Red, hot face. Dry skin. Dilated pupils. Starts and wakes when just falling asleep. Twitchings and jerkings. Quickness of sensations and emotions. Sudden pains, suddenly gone. Convulsions. The delirium of Bell . bites, strikes, wants to escape. Acute attacks in Calcarea children. [ Top ] ZINCUM "Brain troubles during dentition. Child cries out in sleep, rolls head from side to side : face alternately red and pale." Incessant, fidgety feet, must move them constantly. [ Top ] PODOPHYLLUM Pod. has a great desire to press the gums together during dentition. Cholera infantum , stools profuse and gushing : larger than could be expected from amount of food taken : offensive. [ Top ] SULPHUR The Sulphur baby will not remain covered. Rough skin and hair : red lips and eyelids. Redness around anus, hot palms and soles. Acrid stools ( Calc. ) that irritate and inflame wherever they touch the skin. (The urine of Lyc. irritates the parts.) Then the nosodes must not be forgotten in delayed dentition. Burnett proved the value of Tuberculinum in tardy development of all kinds, where there was a family history of deficiency of reaction to tubercle. One has seen a case of delayed dentition in a girl well on in her teens, where, after a dose of Tub. bov. , she erupted eight teeth in a couple of weeks. And one should think of Luet . where the days are happy, but the nights a terror ( Lyc. ) : or Medorrhinum , where the infant rolls over to sleep on its stomach ( Cina ), or a child can only sleep in the knee-elbow position : or the mother has had an evil discharge. [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

[ Top ] COLOCYNTH Doubled up with colic. Pain only relieved by bending double , and pressing into abdomen . [ Top ] CUPRUM METALLICUM Diarrha associated with cramps . Cramps in abdomen, in fingers, calves, feet. [ Top ] CHINA Painless diarrha. Much flatulence. Passes undigested food. [ Top ] VERATRUM ALB. Coldness. COLD SWEAT . Profuse evacuations with profuse, cold sweat . Cold sweat on forehead. [ Top ] ARSENICUM After eating ices ; or cold drinks when hot. After tainted meat and foods or fruit. Relentless vomiting and purging. * * * * * THE GREAT REMEDY FOR PTOMAINE POISONING. [ Top ] CARBO VEG. Diarrha from bad food (like Ars. ) but with more distension. [ Top ] PODOPHYLLUM Excessive evacuations, very offensive : with much flatus, and much colic. [ Top ] PHOS. ACID Like Podoph. But not offensive, and no colic. [ Top ] ALOE Stool urgent : at once after eating. [ Top ] DULCAMARA Diarrha from DAMP, OR DAMP COLD . [ Top ] BAPTISIA Influenzal diarrha : very sudden onset : with prostration, drowsiness, putridity. [ Top ] PYROGEN Rapidly curative in sudden, exhausting summer diarrha ; profuse, watery, painless : extreme restlessness. [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Diarrhoeachildren
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z EPIDEMIC DIARRHA OF CHILDREN : CHOLERA INFANTUM. Aco. * Aeth. * Aloe * Ars. * Bapt. * Bell. * Bry. * Cact. * Camph. * Carbo v. * Cham. * Chin. * Coloc. * Crot. * Cupr. * Dulc. * Ign. * Ipec. * Kreos. * Mag. p. * Merc. * Merc. cor. * Pho. ac. * Phos. * Podo. * Puls. * Pyrog. * Sulph. * Ver. a. Here Homopathy, so rapidly curative in acute disease, gives splendid results. But, of course, the remedy mus be, not only a "homopathic reedy", but homopathic . It must be a remedy not only of diarrha (every drug that can cause diarrha is that), but it must fit the peculiarities of this case of diarrha ; otherwise there is nothing doing. One diarrha reedy will not do for another. A medicine, to cure, must be able to produce just the condition we seek to cure : outside that, no contact is made. Some people might express it, that the vibrations of disease and remedy must be identical -we seem to be approaching that idea. But, however that may be, and whether it is expressed in terms of electricity, or vibration, or Homopathy, so urgent are these cases that one needs their remedies at one's finger-tips, or in portable form for easy reference. But outside the giving of the remedy, the child should be kept warm, and, in desperate cases, when seen first at almost the last grap, we must remember that the infant may have lost more fluid than it can afford to lose and live. Here fluid cannot be retained per rectum , and many a small life may be saved by slow absorption of warm saline, subcutaneously. It is Hahnemann's teaching that not only do different cases of the same disease demand, by their peculiar symptoms, different remedies, but also that different epidemics of the same disease ask for different remedies. And here, in epidemic work, by carefully collecting the symptoms of several individual cases, the genus epidemicus may disclose itself in its entirety, and may be fitted with a medicine which will be found to cure the majority of the cases, even where they do not all display the complete disease picture. But it is also found that in such epidemicus the cases not covered by the epidemic remedy are often very difficult to match. One remembers an epidemic when a number of children came to Out-patients with a diarrha that was painless, while the stools contained much indigested food. Here China quickly put matters right. Colocinth , with its agonies of abdominal pain, that double the victim up, again and again, and demand pressure, would have been useless. To discover the epidemic remedy, whatever it may be, makes prescribing easy and most satisfactory, until -which is possible ! -the type changes- perhaps with the weather, when a fresh remedy has to be sought. [ Top ] MERCURIUS COR. Dysenteric, scanty stools with blood, and incessant straining, not relieved by stool . [ Top ] CUPRUM METALLICUM Diarrha with intense cramps . [ Top ] IPECACUANHA Violent simultaneous vomiting and purging ( Ars. ). Great nausea with pale face and clean tongue. Stools like a mass of fermented yeast. [ Top ] PODOPHYLLUM Diarrha, stools profuse, offensive , gushing, seem to drain the infant dry. Painless. Stools larger than expected from food taken. Desire for much water, none for food. Marked gurgling. Retching ; vomits green froth or food. Diarrha worse in the morning : in teething babies. Head sweats much during sleep. Rectum may prolapse with soft stool. [ Top ] CHINA Painless and undigested stools : copious : putrid. [ Top ] MERCURIUS Slimy, even bloody diarrha : with straining : followed by chilliness. Profuse perspiration which does not relieve. Mouth offensive. Salivation with intense thirst. Tongue large, flabby, tooth-notched. Worse at night : from warmth of bed. Thighs and legs cold and clammy, esp. at night. [ Top ] PHOSPHORUS Characteristic of Phos. thin stool oozes from open anus. Increased urine with diarrha. Or stools large and forcible. In the tall Phos. child : with fear alone -in the dark : thirst for cold water. [ Top ] PULSATILLA Colic and diarrha worse at night. No two stools alike. Relief from fresh air. Mild, weepy children. [ Top ] PHOS. ACID Long-continued diarrha, with cramps ( Cup. ). Stools white ( Calc. ), watery, painless, profuse. Pallid, weary, weedy children. [ Top ] SULPHUR Intolerant of heat : kicks off the clothes : hungry : craves for fat. Great hurry. Stool acrid. Leaves anus red. [ Top ] BAPTISIA Taken suddenly taken and frightfully ill. Sudden attack of diarrha and vomiting, with a rapidly typhoid condition. Ftid, exhausting diarrha, with excoriation. Odour of stool putrid, penetrating. Tongue swollen : dark : dry : yellow or brown centre : cracked : ulcerated. (Comp. Ars. ) Drowsy, as if drugged , or intoxicated. If roused, begins to speak, then fades back into stupor. Dark, red, besotted countenance . Hot -flushed- dusky. Influenzal cases. [ Top ] VERATRUM ALB. Diarrha with violent vomiting : vomit -stools -sweat very profuse . Thirst for much cold water, for acid drinks. Exhaustion after each spell. Cold sweat on forehead from least movement. [ Top ] CARBO VEG. Putrid, or bloody, offensive stools. Acrid. Face pale, or greenish. Abdomen distended : in lumps. Emission of large quantities of flatus. Skin damp, cold : tongue and breath cold . (The Homopathic veritable corpse-reviver.) * * * * * [ Top ] ACONITE From low temperature in room. From chill or fright. Green, watery, frequent stools. Dry heat of body : dry tongue, restlessness and fear. Fear of death. [ Top ] BRYONIA Diarrha from hot weather , and the rectum of hot weather. Vomits food immediately. Colic, with thirst for big drinks, and lumpy diarrha. Dry, parched lips. [ Top ] DULCAMARA Every change of weather to cool , brings diarrha. (Rev. of Bry .) Exposure to cold, or damp. Changeable stools. Nausea with desire for stool. Colic before and during stool. Prostration. [ Top ] CROTON TIG. Yellow, watery stools, come out like a shot , while nursing, or immediately after. Any food or drink starts this sudden stool. A hand pressing on umbilicus produced protrusion of rectum. [ Top ] ALOE Hurry to stool after eating or drinking. Inability to retain -or to evacuate- stool . (Straining may fail to produce stool, which presently slips out unnoticed.) [ Top ] IGNATIA Colic and diarrha in breast-fed infants, whose mothers are suffering from grief. [ Top ] KREOSOTUM Cholera infantum in teething infants, with very painful dentition : gums painful, spongy. Severe cases, with incessant vomiting, and stools cadaveric-smelling. Intensely irritable ( Cham. ). (See HOMOPATHY , June, 1934, pp. 178-9.) [ Top ] CHAMOMILLA Watery, greenish stools : excoriating : smell like rotten eggs. Very cross ( Kreos. ). Must be carried. Especially in teething babies. [ Top ] CACTUS Bilious diarrha, preceded by great pain. Great weight in anus ; desire to pass a quantity, but nothing comes. [ Top ] BELLADONNA Drowsiness ( Baptisia ) with dry, burning heat. Pupils dilated. Stools green, small, frequent. Colic before stool : straining. Child starts with every noise : twitches. [ Top ] COLOCYNTH Paroxysms of severe colicky pain precede stools. Immediately after eating. Relief from doubling up and pressure . Frothy stools. Stools watery, then bilious, then bloody ; excoriating ; frequent ; not profuse. [ Top ] MAGNESIA PHOS. Very like Colocynth , but urgently demands heat as well as pressure . (A case in Hospital : Colocynth had helped the diarrha, but the Resident thought the child would die. The only relief was from a warm hand pressed on abdomen. Magn. phos. saved the child.) SEVERE URGEN CASES, WITH COLLAPSE. [ Top ] ÆTHUSA Intolerance of milk. Face expresses anxiety and pain. Linea nasalis -pearly whiteness on upper lip, bounded by a distinct line to angles of mouth. Violent vomiting : of milk : after milk. Stool undigested : thin : green : bilious. Violent straining before and after stool. Collapse -almost as bad as Ars. only not restless . A remedy of violence -violent vomiting- violent convulsions -violent pains- violent diarrha. [ Top ] ARSENICUM Worse at night, 1 to 3 A. M. Rapid emaciation ; exhaustion and collapse . Intense restlessness . ( Pyrog. ) (Opp. of Æth. ) Painless, offensive, watery stools. There may be simultaneous vomiting and diarrha. ( Ipec. ) After cold drinks ; when heated ; in older persons after ices. Thirst for cold water, immediately vomited. Coldness of extremities. Pale cadaverous face. Skin dry, wrinkled, toneless. [ Top ] CAMPHOR Skin cold as marble . ( Carbo veg. ), but child will not remain covered . Great prostration and diarrha. [ Give a drop of the strong tincture on sugar. Repeat in 5 to 15 minutes if case urgent. Keep Camphor away from Homopathic medicines .] [ Top ] PYROGEN Extreme restlessness : has to keep on moving. Only momentary relief from moving, but has to move for that relief. (Comp. Rhus ) Diarrha with frightfully offensive stools ( Bapt. ). Profuse, watery, painless stools, with (?) vomiting. (One has seen Pyrogen almost magic for sudden, very exhausting attacks of summer diarrha.) [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Diphtheria
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z DIPHTHERIA. Apis * Ars. * Bapt. * Diph. * Kali bi. * Lac. c. * Lach. * Lyc. * Merc. cy. * Phyt. [ Top ] APIS Throat bright-red, puffy, "varnished." Uvula long ; dematous. Nothing must touch throat ( Lach. ). [ Top ] ARSENICUM Membrane looks dry, shrivelled. The Arsenicum anxiety, restlessness and prostration are present. Worse at night : 1-2 A. M. Chilliness : incessant thirst for small quantities. [ Top ] BAPTISIA Putridity : with dull red face ; drowsiness ; patient as if drugged. Membrane dark : dry brown tongue. [ Top ] DIPHTHERINUM When the attack from the onset tends to malignancy. Painless diphtheria. Symptoms almost, or entirely objective. Patient weak, apathetic. Stupor. Dark-red swelling of tonsils and throat. Breath and discharges very offensive ( Merc. cy. ). Membrane thick, dark-grey or brownish black. Temperature low, or subnormal. Pulse weak and rapid. Vital reaction very low. Epistaxis, or profound prostration from the onset. Collapse almost at the very beginning. Swallows without pain, but fluids are vomited or returned through nose. Laryngeal diphtheria ; post-diphtheric paralysis. ( Caust. , Cocc. , Gels. and Lycopodium .). When the patient from the first seems doomed, and the most carefully- selected remedies fail to relieve, or permanently improve. To remove persistent diphtheria-organisms, in "carriers." Like all the nosodes, it is practically worthless below the 30th potency while its curative virtues increase with the higher potencies. It should not be repeated too frequently. [ Top ] KALI BICH. Nasal diphtheria : ropy discharges. Exudation tough and firmly adherent. [ Top ] LAC CANINUM Patients nervous, imaginative, highly sensitive. Skin hypersensitive ( Lach. ). Touch unbearable, though hard pressure gives no pain. Membrane pearly, or silver white. Milky coating on tongue. Characteristic feature is alternation of sides . Pain will jump back and forth from side to side. [ Top ] LACHESIS Membrane starts on left side, spreads to right. Face and throat look cyanotic. Choking. Cold things more easily swallowed than hot. Great sensitiveness of neck and throat, so that patient cannot stand the touch of bedclothes, and pulls neck of night attire open. General and local aggravation from heat, and all symptoms are worse after sleep. The longer the sleep, the worse he is on waking. Characteristics are loquacity and suspicion. [ Top ] LYCOPODIUM Patient worse from 4 to 8 P. M. Starts in nose ( Kali bic. ) or right side throat, spreads to left. Warm drinks more easily swallowed : but reverse sometimes the case. Movement of nostrils. Diminished urine or copious sediment of urates, or fine red sand. [ Top ] MERCURIUS CY. Fairly rapid onset, with prostration. One or both sides of throat affected. Membrane spreads rapidly over entire throat. Colour white, yellow, or greenish. Tongue thickly coated, moist ; salivation. Odour always putrid. Hot sweats. Tepid liquids better swallowed than hot or cold. Patient (generally) worse late evening and night. Has also proved curative in Vincent's Angina. [ Top ] PHYTOLACCA Frequently indicated. Membrane grey or white, may start on uvula. May spread from right tonsil to left ( Lyc. ). But, unlike Lyc. , the pain is worse from heat. Fauces dark-red : complains of lump in throat ; or as if red-hot ball had stuck in throat. Pain goes to ear. [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Dysentery
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z SOME REMEDIES OF ACUTE DYSENTERY. Aco. * Aloe * Apis * Ars. * Canth. * Caps. * Carbo v. * Colch. * Coloc. * Cupr. * Gels. * Ipec. * Merc. * Merc. cor. * Nux * Phos. * Podo. * Psor. * Rhus * Sulph. * Ver. a. [ Top ] MERCURIUS COR. Persistent straining before, during, and after stool (Rev. of Nux ). Scanty stools of bloody or shreddy slime. Stools excoriate, burn. Burning in rectum. "Never-get-done" sensation. Straining to pass hot urine, drop by drop. Merc. cor. IS ALMOST A SPECIFIC FOR DYSENTERY . Tongue large, flabby, tooth-notched. Mouth foul. Salivation. [ Top ] MERCURIUS Bloody, slimy stools with much straining : never-get-done feeling ( Merc. cor. ) ; but Merc. cor. has a more violent attack. Stools followed by chilliness. Rarely indicated where there is no slime. Rarely indicated where the tongue is dry. "Your first prescription should cure in epidemic dysentery, and if you work cautiously you will cure every case." - KENT. [ Top ] ALOE "Violent tenesmus, heat in rectum, prostration to fainting and profuse clammy sweats." Bloody mucus passes after urging and straining. Rumbling, gurgling, sudden urge to stool. Urine and fæces pass at the same time : cannot pass one without the other ( Mur. a. ). Curious symptom. Stools, even solid, pass unnoticed. Sense of insecurity at anus. Another curious verified symptom. On laying head on pillow, as if a fine globe broke at base of brain, fragments could be heard tinkling as they fell. [ Top ] NUX VOMICA Stools of slimy mucus and blood, but small and unsatisfactory : with relief, pro tem., after every stool (Rev. of Merc. and Merc. cor. ). Irregular peristalsis. Griping pains, now here, now there, in abdomen. COLIC . Nux is irritable, hypersensitive, offended. Is chilly, with great aversion to uncovering. [ Top ] COLOCYNTH With much colic, only relieved by bending double , and pressing hard into abdomen . [ Top ] SULPHUR Stools bloody with constant straining : with the Merc. "never-get-done" sensation. Dysenteric stools, esp. at night, with colic and violent tenesmus. "Follows Nux , esp. when worse at night : discharge of blood, slime, pus, with fever." Pain so violent as to cause nausea and drenching perspiration. Stools acrid : excoriate. Characteristic symptom, redness about anus . [ Top ] PHOSPHORUS Dysenteric stools oozing from an open anus. Patient craves COLD DRINKS and food ; ices. [ Top ] APIS Stools with every motion of body as if anus constantly open ( Phos. ) ; oozes blood. "Tomato-sauce" stools-blood, mucus, food. Thirstless : can't bear heat-warm room. [ Top ] IPECACUANHA Dysentery with constant nausea . Sits almost constantly on stool and passes a little slime, or a little bright-red blood . Tenesmus awful : pain so great that nausea comes on and he vomits bile. Tongue clean with nausea . [ Top ] COLCHICUM Dysentery in the fall of the year, when days are warm and nights cold ( Dulc. ). Stools : shreddy and bloody like scrapings : thin, watery, but they cool to form a jelly. Great meteoric distension ( Carbo veg. ). Bloody discharges from bowels with deathly nausea. The smell of food causes nausea to faintness. [ Top ] GELSEMIUM Epidemic dysentery, malarial or catarrhal. Acute catarrhal enteritis, mucous diarrha. Discharges almost involuntary : intense spasmodic colic and tenesmus. Fright, emotion, anticipation will produce diarrha ( Arg. nit. ). Gels. has chills up and down back : trembling ; and heaviness of limbs and eyelids. [ Top ] ARSENICUM RESTLESSNESS, ANGUISH, FEARFUL ANXIETY . Worse after midnight. Burning thirst for sips of cold water. Internal, violent burning pain, with cold extremities. Better heat, hot drinks . (Rev. of Phos. ) Great collapse and prostration. Tongue dry, to brown, or black. Putrid stools : involuntary : with prostration : blood and straining. THE GREAT REMEDY IN PTOMAINE POISONING . (N. B.- "Don't give Ars. in dysentery unless there is the Ars. Restlessness, anxiety, and thirst for frequent small drinks.") [ Top ] RHUS TOX. Cases with extreme restlessness ( Ars. ). Worse damp weather : damp cold weather . Dry, dark-coated tongue : or triangular red tip. Herpetic eruptions about mouth. Copious, watery, bloody stools ; drive him out of bed ( Sulph. ) as early as 4 A. M. "Diarrha with tearing pains running down back of leg with every stool. Painful tenesmus with every stool." [ Top ] ACONITE Stools of pure blood, with a little slime. With anguish, cramp, terrible urging. Or black, very fetid stools. Sensation, warm fluid escaping from anus. [ Top ] CUPRUM METALLICUM Frightful colic ; > pressure. Spouting stool of bloody, greenish water. Cramps-abdomen, calves, soles, fingers, toes. Strong metallic taste. [ Top ] PODOPHYLLUM "Abdomen becomes tumultuous." Gurgling : then sudden, profuse, putrid stools : generally painless : with perhaps prolapsus recti. [ Top ] PSORINUM Stools dark, gushing, horridly putrid. Worse at night. Patient greasy, offensive. Cases which do not respond to apparently indicated remedy ( Tub. ). [ Top ] CAPSICUM Small frequent stools of blood and mucus. After stool tenesmus and thirst : but drinking causes shuddering. Thirst after every dysenteric stool : sudden craving for ice-cold water, which causes chilliness. Violent tenesmus in rectum and bladder at the same time ( Canth. ). Smarting and burning in anus and rectum. ( Caps. burnings are like cayenne pepper.) Typical Caps. is plump, flabby, sensitive to cold : red, cold face : nose red and cold. [ Top ] CANTHARIS Stools like scrapings of intestines. Great burning : burning at anus. Tenesmus in rectum and bladder ( Caps. ). "It is a singular fact that if there be frequent micturition with burning cutting pain attending the flow, Cantharis is almost always the remedy for whatever other sufferings there may be." [ Top ] CARBO VEG. "No matter what the trouble is, in Carbo veg. there is always burning." Diarrha, dysentery, cholera, with bloody watery stool. Watery mucus mixed with blood. Stools horribly putrid, with putrid flatulence. The more thin, dark, bloody mucus there is, the better the remedy is indicated. Anus red ( Sulph. ), raw, bleeding, itching. Cold breath, cold sweat, cold nose. Internal burning with external coldness. Coldness and collapse, with air hunger . [ Top ] VERATRUM ALB. Colic : burning, twisting, constricting, cutting. Distension, tenderness. Stools frequent ; watery, greenish ; blackish ; bloody. Involuntary when passing flatus : from least movement of body. May be simultaneous stool and vomiting ( Ars. ). Sunken, hippocratic face. Characteristic symptom, cold sweat on forehead . (One of Hahnemann's great cholera medicines.) The straining is not marked in Verat. [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Dysmenorrhoea
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z SOME REMEDIES OF DYSMENORRHEA WITH INDICATIONS. Aco. * Actea * Bell. * Cact. * Calc. * Calc. p. * Caul. * Caust. * Cham. * Cocc. * Coloc. * Con. * Croc. * Cupr. * Cycl. * Gels. * Graph. * Ign. * Kali c. * Lyc. * Mag. m. * Mag. p. * Med. * Nux m. * Plat. * Puls. * Sep. * Sulph. * Tuber. * Ver. a. * Vib. op. [ Top ] MAGNESIA PHOS. Sudden paroxysms of pain, with or before flow. Worse cold. Better warmth : hot applications. Better pressure : bending double ( Coloc .) [ Top ] COLOCYNTH Waves of violent, cutting, grasping, clutching, cramping pain. Paroxysms grow in intensity. Better for hard pressure : from doubling up ( Mag. phos. ), from heat ( MAG. PHOS. ). Bends over back of chair : doubles up hard on her fists. Turns and twists : cannot keep still. Screams with pain. Perhaps increasing nausea : vomits and retches. Especially where the pain is caused by vexation. [ Top ] ACONITE Labour-like pressing in uterus. Has to bend double, but no position relieves. After a fright and vexation, during menses : to prevent suppression. Ovaritis from suddenly checked flow. Menses suppressed by getting feet wet ( Puls ., Sil .), or cold bath during M. P. Sharp shooting pain more to right of fundus abdomen exceedingly sensitive. But -always the Aconite condition : -fear fear of death : extreme restlessness and anxiety. [ Top ] PULSATILLA Violent menstrual colic : bends double : distended abdomen. Throws the covers off : wants windows open. Tearful : causeless weeping. Dating from getting feet wet ( Acon ., Sil .) : or suppression from getting feet wet. ( Rhus ). Where menses are scanty, especially, and have started late. [ Top ] MEDORRHINUM Intense menstrual colic. Knees drawn up. Terrible bearing down, labour-like pains. Must press feet against support. Breasts cold as ice during M. P. [ Top ] BELLADONNA Violent contraction of circular fibres ( Cact .), "as if uterus were clutched with a string". Hour-glass contractions. "As if tightened." Pains come suddenly, and go suddenly. Bearing down (better standing), followed by a gush. Menses bright red : or dark ? - fluid with clots : - HOT . Bell. is flushed : hot : twitches and jerks. Thirsty, especially for lemonade. [ Top ] CACTUS A young plethoric vigorous woman comes down violently with congestion of the uterus at the menstrual period. She screams because of the violent clutching and cramping of the uterus. The circular fibres clutch ( Bell .) "as if a tape were tied round the organ." It fills with clots, and the spasm to expel them is like a labour pain, and she screams again-till the flow becomes free enough to give relief. "Suffocative attacks, because constriction of heart will commonly go along with constriction of the uterus." - KENT. [ Top ] VIBURNUM OP. (Cramp Bark) Neuralgic and spasmodic dysmenorrha. Excruciating colic, sudden onset, in uterus and lower abdomen, just preceding menses. Or, pain begins in back, goes round loins to pubis, like labour pains. There may be large clots, solid like liver. (A great remedy for threatened abortion, with cramps in abdomen and legs.) [ Top ] CUPRUM METALLICUM "All the sphincters are convulsive." Agonizing colic before or during menses : or after suppression, by cold bathing during M. P. ( Acon .) : from suppressed foot-sweat. Violent unbearable cramps in abdomen, extending to chest, causing nausea, vomiting ; sometimes convulsions of limbs, with piercing shrieks. Cuprum cramps usually start in fingers and toes. [ Top ] CAULOPHYLUM (Squaw root) "Heads the list for uterine spasms." Spasmodic dysmenorrha. : spasmodic pains in bladder, stomach, groins, even chest and limbs : congestion of uterus. Pains fly about. "Menses preceded by pain in small of back, bitter taste, vertigo, chilliness ; flow scanty with intense nausea and vomiting of bile." [ Top ] GELSEMIUM Heavy sore uterus : feels grasped ( Cact ., Bell .). Menses with vertigo, sick headache, vomiting, congestion to head, deep-red face. Characteristics : Chills up and down back, with heaviness of limbs and eyelids. [ Top ] COCCULUS Cutting and cramping pains on appearance of menses. Uterine cramps. Menses appear seven or fourteen days too early, with violent colic. As if inner parts suffering from sharp pressure of a stone : worse motion, stooping, even sitting. Flow lessens during spasm : copious as pain abates (Compare Cycl .) M. P. too plus and too frequent : gushes when she rises to her feet. In women prostrated with anxiety or grief. From prolonged loss of sleep, menses too frequent, copious, and prolonged. [ Top ] CYCLAMEN M. P. profuse, early : black and clotted membranous. Labour-like pains small of back, run down sides of abdomen to pubes, every few minutes, during which no discharge occurs ( Cocc .). After attacks blood more watery. Sees stars all the time with dim vision. [ Top ] CAUSTICUM At time for flow to start, violent cramp-like pains. Before M. P., weakness and melancholy. Menses flow only by day : leucorrha only by night. Caust . is worse cold dry winds and weather. Better for cold water. [ Top ] CHAMOMILLA Pains of a very severe and aggravating nature. Hot and thirsty with the pain. CANNOT BEAR IT ! Sudden spiteful or uncivil irritability. Excessively sensitive to pain : makes her mad. Menses too early, clotted, black, offensive. Membraneous dysmenorrha. [ Top ] IGNATIA Menses irregular : scanty : with violent spasms and pains : from irritation of nervous system, not from uterine congestion. Uterine spasms, with labour-like pains. Apprehensive : sadness and sighing : unhappy love with silent grief. Sensitive : hyperacute feeling. Incredible changes of mood ( Croc ., Puls .). The sighing remedy : remedy of contradictions. Everything as you would not expect it. Does unaccountable and most unexpected things. [ Top ] NUX MOSCHATA Distressing dysmenorrha from exposure to cold, or living in damp house. With this, dry mouth and thirstlessness. Wakes with " tongue cleaving to roof of mouth." Falls asleep on all occasions : cannot keep awake. Seems in a dream : dazed and automatic. [ Top ] VERATRUM ALB. Despair, before M. P. : everything black. During M. P. becomes cold as death : lips blue extremities cold and blue : dreadful pains. Sinking : - (?) mania to kiss everybody. Coldness ; copious sweat, vomiting, diarrha. Cold sweat on forehead. [ Top ] MAGNESIA MUR. Profuse, dark, lumpy menses : like pitch with cramps, backache, pain in thighs. Backache relieved by pressing back hard on chair, or lying on a hard pillow ( Nat. mur. ). Bearing-down pains ( Sep ., Lil. t. , etc.). Mag mur . is worse for sea bathing, salt baths, salt. [ Top ] PLATINA Menses too early ; too profuse ; too short lasting : may be thick, tough, black like tar. Extreme sensitiveness of ext. (and int.) genitals "not inflammation, hyperesthesia." "Curious mental symptoms : feels tall, other people and objects look small (Rev. Hyos .). The Pharisee among drugs. Contemptuous mood. Arrogant and haughty. Pride and over-estimation of self. Illusions : everything seems small, and all persons mentally and physically inferior. Bandaged and numb sensations. [ Top ] CROCUS Menses profuse ; dark, clotted, stringy, viscid. The hemorrhages of Crocus , from whatever organ-come away in long black strings, hanging from the bleeding orifice. Sensation of something alive and jumping about in abdomen [ One remembers a hospital patient trying to tell the gynecologist (who did not recognize the symptoms and laughed at it) that she felt as if she had something alive in her abdomen. ] ( Thuja ). The Crocus patient is even more emotional and changeable than Puls . Rapid alternations of excitement and liveliness, with anger and depression. Jumps, dances, sings ; very affectionate : then sudden anger and rage. "Very unusual vacillation of mood." [ Top ] GRAPHITES Menses pale, scanty, late with violent colic, or irregular with pitchy black discharge. Bleeding piles, or blood from throat or bronchi when M. P. should appear : -like a vicarious menstruation ( Bry .). M. P. late, painful, scanty : takes cold, or has morning sickness, or sweats during M. P. Graph . is worse COLD ; during menses ; from suppressions. (?) with stomach or skin troubles. [ Top ] KALI CARB. Uterine spasms with profuse menses : with heavy, aching weight in small of back. Menses acrid, pungent, excoriate thighs. Incessant oozing in pale waxy women. Intermittent pulse. Pains stitch and jerk. It was suggested, "Look up Crocus ", which proved to be the remedy. At hey next visit she came across to say, "I could thank you on my knees for that medicine !" It had relieved or cured whatever the condition complained of. Queer symptoms often suggest a remedy which, when looked up, is found to correspond with the rest of the symptoms, and therefore cures. [ Top ] TUBERCULINUM May be needed in any menstrual difficulty or suffering, where there is a T. B. history. [ Top ] CONIUM Uterine spasms during too early and scanty menses. Suppressed menses : -painful. Throbbing, burning, tearing pains. Characteristics : vertigo, worse turning head. At every M. P. breasts enlarged and painful. Induration of uterus : has cured fibroids. [ Top ] LYCOPODIUM Menstrual disturbances : dysmenorrha. Absence or suppression of M. P. for many months, patient withered, sallow, feeble. When first M. P. fails to appear till 15 to 18, without development. Dysmenorrha in a Lyc . Patient, i. e. At slightest joy, weeps : weeps if thanked. Afternoon and evening aggravation of symptoms, especially 4-8 aggravation : desires sweets : hot drinks. Anticipation is distressing. [ Top ] CALCAREA PHOS. "Suffered since first menses : went swimming or got feet wet ( Puls .) : has suffered since." "Undeveloped." A state of undevelopment, a stenosis : horrible menstrual colic. "Bearing down pains, as if everything would escape ( Sepia , etc.). Doubles up : better heat : worse cold" ( Mag ., Phos ., Coloc .). [ Top ] ACTEA (CIMICIFUGA) Menstrual disorders in hysterical and rheumatic constitutions. Irregularity : flow copious ; suppressed ; scanty. The more the flow the greater the pain. Sufferings during the flow, as a rule. With mental symptoms ; rheumatic symptoms ; jerking and cramping ; sleeplessness. "Rheumatic dysmenorrha." Uterine pains dart from side to side. During M. P. hysteric or epileptic spasms. Bearing down pain : better lying down. Cold and chilly : must wrap up. Cimic . thinks she is going crazy. Sadness and gloom come over her like a cloud. [ Top ] CALCAREA M. P. too soon, lasts too long, too profuse and least excitement may cause a return. Cramps. Labour-like pains abdomen and back : with many symptoms mental and physical... but IN A Calcarea PATIENT : Chilly, with much sweating : sweating, feet, etc., when cold. Head and neck sweat at night. Calc . is obstinate ; tired ; sensitive to cold. Abounds in fears. Sensitive to cruelty. Craves eggs. Generally tends to grow fat, with poor vitality. In regard to its menstrual symptoms, KENT says (even with these) Calcarea is not always indicated : not unless all the symptoms go together to make up the Calcarea patient. Sometimes it may occur to your mind to say, that with five or six keynotes, certainly you would give Calcarea : but suppose you did have five or six keynotes of Calcarea , and the patient should be a Pulsatilla patient, would you expect to cure her with Calcarea ? Supposing the patient always avoided warm things and much clothing, and wanted the cold open air, and still had a dozen keynotes, you would find every time that Calcarea would fail. Unless you combine the particulars with the things that are general, and the generals with the particulars, unless the remedy fits the patient from within out, generally and particularly, a cure need not be expected. That is why I say, do not prescribe on keynotes, but upon the symptoms of the patient. [ Top ] SEPIA Most violent dysmenorrha in delicate sallow girls. Menstrual symptoms of all sorts : menses scanty, or profuse. When child ceases to nurse and menses do not reappear, to establish the flow. But in the Sepia patient : cold, indifferent, wants to get away and be quiet. "Bearing down pain" characteristic. [ Top ] SULPHUR Dysmenorrha : spasmodic pain in hypogastrium, as if intestines strung up in knots. Scanty flow : colicky pain small of back : but in a Sulph . patient : untidy : argumentative. Loves fat-sweets : hungry at in A. M. Uncovers or puts feet out. [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Enuresis
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z THE MORE COMMON REMEDIES OF ENURESIS WITH INDICATIONS. Apis * Arg. n. * Ars. * Bell. * Caust. * Cina * Dulc. * Equis. * Hep. * Kreos. * Lyc. * Nat. m. * Nux m. * Phos. * Psor. * Puls. * Rhus * Sep. * Staph. * Sulph. * Thuj. [ Top ] CAUSTICUM Caust. has weakness or paralysis of single parts ; - paralysis of face, or of anus, or of bladder, etc. Expectoration slips back. Or anus prolapses on coughing. Or urine spurts on coughing. Paresis of vocal cords. "Unconscious of urine as it passes" ( Apis , Arg. n. , Cup. , Mag. m. , Sars. ) ( Aloe , of stool). Urinates so easily that he is not sensible of the tream." Useful in children who wet the bed, especially in first sleep ( Sepia , Kreos. ). Typical Caust. is worse for cold dry weather and winds . ( Rhus and Dulc. worse cold wet ). "Worse in clear fine weather : better in wet weather." Worse changes of the weather. [ Top ] SEPIA Sepia is compelled to keep her mind on the neck of the bladder, or she will lose her urine." Involuntary urine as soon as the child goes to sleep at night. The bed is wet almost as soon as the child goes to sleep ( Caust. , Kreos. ). Typical Sepia is sallow : indifferent : hates sympathy ; wants to get away alone. (Comp. Nat. mur. ). [ Top ] KREOSOTUM Sudden urging to urinate : can't go quick enough ( Petroselinum ). Sudden urging during first, very profound sleep : ( Caust. , Sepia ) wets the bed. Frequent urging : at night can't get out of bed quick enough. Wakes with urging, but cannot retain urine, or dreams he is urinating and wets bed ( Bell. ). Urine flows during first ( Sep. ) deep sleep, from which the child is roused with difficulty. [ Top ] APIS Incontinence of urine with great irritation of the parts. Worse night and from coughing. (It may have, also, incontinence of stool, as if anus were constantly open. Phos. ). Typical Apis is apathetic, indifferent, joyless, jealous. Its pains burn and sting . Intolerance of heat . Thirstless ( Puls. ). [ Top ] PULSATILLA Involuntary micturition : urine dribbles while sitting (Compare Nat. mur. ) or walking, while coughing ( Caust. ), passing wind : at night in bed, especially in little girls. As "Enuresis noctura for 2 years in a girl of 5 1/2, of mild disposition, fair, frequently changing colour." Especially after Measles : worse in autumn. Typical Puls. is changeable and fickle : touchy and weepy. Loves fuss and sympathy. Worse heat : stuffy room : fat and rich food. Better moving about in the open air. [ Top ] BELLADONNA "No remedy has greater irritation in bladder and along urinary tract than Bell. " ( Staph. ). Constant urging : dribbles : burns ( Staph. ) like fire along whole length of urethra. Spasmodic retention, or involuntary passage. During sleep, dribbling of urine. Dreams of passing urine, and involuntarily passes it ( Kreos. ). Dribbling when standing or walking : or from mere motion, urine spurts ( Puls. ). (Reverse of Rhus ). When cold or chilled, they lose their urine ( Dulc. , Rhus , Caust. ). Starts in sleep, and wets the bed. [ Top ] STAPHISAGRIA Teasing and tearing all night long : bloody urine : involuntary urine, acrid and corroding ; with burning ( Bell. ). Worse from motion (Reverse of Rhus ). In young women after marriage : in old men with prostatic troubles, continued teasing with dribbling ( Bell. ). After urination feels bladder not empty, for urine continues to dribble away. Staph. is a great remedy of sphincters : for sphincters stretched during operations. Also the great remedy of suppressed anger, suppressed feelings. Irritable bladder after suppressed wrath ; after insults. "Great indignation about things done by others or by himself." Hypersensitive spots and areas ; little points. "Whole mind and nervous system are in a fret." [ Top ] LYCOPODIUM Involuntary urination during sleep . "A marked feature of Lyc. is polyuria during the night . Passes enormous quantities of clear urine : by day, quantity normal." Urine dribbles away, afternoon and evening, after 4 P. M. Urine reddens and irritates skin : especially babies, - if left in contact. Another leading symptom, RED SAND IN URINE : on child's diaper. Typical Lyc. craves sweets, sugar ; hot drinks ; has afternoon or evening aggravation of symptoms : especially 4-8 P. M. Lyc. is more alive mentally than physically. "Ugly on waking", otherwise better in the mornings. May have the curious symptom, weeps when thanked. [ Top ] EQUISETUM Enuresis day and night ; profuse, watery urine : especially enuresis from habit. Has many urinary troubles. Pain in bladder as from distension : tenderness. Constant desire to urinate and pass large quantities of pale urine without relief. "Rapidly restored control over stools and urine in an old woman with general paralysis." [ Top ] ARGENTUM NITRICUM Urine passed unconsciously and uninterruptedly. Spasmodic enuresis at night : (by day too). Typical Arg. nit. craves sugar - which disagrees : craves salt ; cool, open air : is worse in high places. [ Top ] HEPAR "Urine passes very slowly, drops perpendicularly, is not voided with force. If with this you find wetting of the bed at night, Hepar is the remedy." [ Top ] CINA Urine copious and involuntary : with worm symptoms and ravenous appetite. Typical Cina is cross and "ugly" : wants to be carried : or won't be looked at or touched. Wants things and throws them away. Bores into nose with fingers. Urine turns milky on standing. [ Top ] NATRUM MUR. Involuntary escape of urine while walking, coughing or sneezing ( Caust. , Puls. ). Violent desire and inability to retain urine. ( Sulph. ). Whenever he sat down urine came away (Compare Puls. ) : day and night ; necessitating very frequent change of clothing and bed-clothes : continual craving for salt. Has to wait long for urine to pass ( Lyc. ) especially if others are near by. Morbid appetite for salt ( Phos. , Nit. a. , etc.). Typical Nat. mur. : mapped tongue : herpes about lips : crack middle lower lip. Better alone : hates sympathy : maddening headaches. After malaria and much quinine . [ Top ] SULPHUR Constant desire to urinate : a few drops pass involuntarily. Nocturnal enuresis. Sudden, imperative desire, if not gratified urine passes involuntarily ( Thuj. , Nat. m. , Kreos. ). Irresistible desire to urinate on seeing water running from a hydrant ( Canth. , Lyssin .). Must rise at night to urinate : rushes away from work to relieve bladder, or wets clothes. "Enuresis in pale, lean children, with large abdomen, who love sugar and highly-seasoned food, and abhor to be washed" ( Phos. ). Hungry at 11 A. M. Won't be covered at night. [ Top ] THUJA Involuntary urination at night or when coughing ( Caust. ). Got up at least six times nightly : saturated the bed frequently : urine highly coloured, strong odour. Incontinence of urine ( Sulph. , Nat. mur. , Kreos. , etc.) : sudden desire, unable to retain it without grasping penis. Cannot hold urine when riding, or during a long walk ( Bell. ). Chronic incontinence from paralysis of sphincter. After vaccination. From tea-drinking. Drops in sleep : worse onions (? Warts, etc.). [ Top ] DULCAMARA If chilled must hurry to urinate . Bladder troubles better in summer : worse in winter. Involuntary urination after wading in cold water. Typically : worse cold wet weather ; suppressed discharges, sweat, etc. (Comp. Rhus ; rev. Caust. ). [ Top ] RHUS TOX. Urine involuntary at night : when at rest (Reverse of Bell. ). Weakness of bladder in girls and women, with frequent desire to urinate. Constant dribbling in boys. Dribbling of urine in cold air , and on becoming very cold. (Compare Dulc. ). May be violent tenesmus of bladder, with dribbling of bloody drops. Typical Rhus is much affected by Damp and cold : by washing ( Sulph. , Psor. ). Better for heat. Relieved by motion ( Puls. ). [ Top ] NUX MOSCHATA Incontinence of urine. Typical Nux mosch . is worse from COLD : ( Dulc. , Rhus , Ars. ) from cold winds, draughts, drinks, bath. Is indifferent, apathetic, automatic, drowsy, with dry mouth and no thirst. [ Top ] ARSENICUM Involuntary micturition, and bed-wetting. Typical Ars. is nervous and anxious : restless : fastidious ( Nux ). "Will get out of bed to put a chair straight." Very chilly . Its worst hour, 1-2 A. M. - thereabouts. [ Top ] PHOSPHORUS Involuntary urination in children of the Phos. build, who grow too rapidly. Typical Phos. craves salt : cold drinks : ices. Fears the dark, being alone, ghosts, thunder. The Phos. build is tall and slender : fine hair. May pass copious, watery, colourless urine. [ Top ] PSORINUM Vesical paresis. Obstinate cases of enuresis : wets the bed : during full moon. Typical Psor. is chilly. Dreads washing ( Sulph. ) : is greasy and "offensive to sight and smell." [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Erysipelas
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z ERYSIPELAS. Aco. * Ammon. c. * Apis * Arn. * Ars. * Bapt. * Bell. * Canth. * Crot. h. * Crot. t. * Cupr. * Euphor. * Graph. * Hep. * Hippoz. * Lach. * Merc. * Puls. * Rhus * Sec. c. * Sulph. * Thuj. * Ver. v. [ Top ] ACONITE Sudden violent onset after exposure to cold wind. Intense fever, with restlessness, and fear of death . [ Top ] APIS May be in patches. Great tumefaction. High degree of inflammation, with stinging, burning , and dema and vesication. Eyelids like sacs of water. Amelioration from cold ; aggravation from heat Fidgety, nervous, fretful : sleepless. [ Top ] ARSENICUM "Sudden inflammatory conditions like gangrenous and erysipelatous inflammations. A sudden inflammation that tends to produce malignancy in the part, belongs to Arsenicum ." The secretions of Arsen. are acrid. Characteristic, burnings relieved by heat : intense anxiety, restlessness and prostration. [ Top ] BAPTISIA Drowsy, dusky, comatose ; face dark-red, with besotted expression. May be roused, but falls asleep answering. Typhoid conditions, in the course of disease. Acts very rapidly ; rapid collapse, and rapid restoration. ( Crot. h. ) [ Top ] BELLADONNA Swelling, smooth, bright-red, streaked red ; or deep, dark red. Not much tendency to dema or vesication. Pains are throbbing ; throbbing in brain. Brain affected. Cases with delirium. Jerking of limbs. Belladonna is acute, sudden , and violent. Belladonna is red, and intensely hot, dry. [ Top ] CANTHARIS Erysipelas of face with large blisters. Burning in eyes : whole atmosphere looks yellow : scalding tears. Like Rhus , but when very violent, Canth. will be indicated. " Rhus has the blisters and the burning, but in Canth. between your two visits the erysipelas has grown black : it is a dusky rapid change that has taken place, looks as if gangrene would set in. Burning like fire from touch : as if the finger were a coal of fire. Not so in Rhus . "The little blisters, if touched, burn like fire. Eruptions burn when touched " (KENT). Erysipelas of eyes, with gangrenous tendency. "Unquenchable thirst with disgust for drinks." [ Top ] CROTALUS HORRIDUS Frequently recurring erysipelas of face. General local phlegmonous or dematous erysipelas. Skin bluish-red ; low fever. Gangrene : skin separated from muscles by a fetid fluid. Black spots with red areola and dark, blackish redness of adjacent tissues. " Crotalus is indicated in disease of the very lowest, the most putrid type, coming on with unusual rapidity, reaching that putrid state in an unusually short time" (KENT). ( Bapt. ). [ Top ] CROTON TIG. " Erysipelas that itches very much ." "Eruptions that itch very much ; but cannot bear to scratch, as it hurts. A very slight scratch, a mere rub, serves to allay the irritation" (GUERNSEY). Sensation, "Insects creeping on face." "Cough disappears and the eruption comes ; then eruption goes and cough comes back." [ Top ] CUPRUM METALLICUM Erysipelas of face disappears suddenly. Eruptions "strike in" and cramps, spasms, Convulsions supervene . To bring the eruption back, with relief. Cramps begin characteristically in fingers and toes. [ Top ] EUPHORBIUM Vesicular erysipelas : erysipelas bulbosum. Red inflammatory swelling, with vesicles as large as peas, filled with yellow liquid . Red inflammatory swelling, with boring, grinding, gnawing from gums into ear, followed by itching and tingling. Vesicles burst and emit a "yellow humour." Shuddering and chilliness. Temporary attacks of craziness. [ Top ] HIPPOZÆNINUM (Nosode of Glanders) "Malignant erysipelas, particularly if attended by large formation of pus, and destruction of parts . Ulcers with not disposition to heal, livid appearance" (CLARKE). [ Top ] LACHESIS Purple, mottled, puffy. "When the cerebral condition does not yield to Belladonna ". Bell. Is red : Lach. less red and more blue . Especially affects the left side. Lachesis , typically, is worse after sleep : is loquacious-suspicious jealous. Is hypersensitive to touch, esp. on throat ; wants face free, or suffocates. [ Top ] MERCURIUS With salivation : bitter or salt taste. With offensiveness : breath, sweat . Erysipelas with sloughing : with "brown mortification." With burning : ulceration. Chilliness and heat alternately : or heat and shuddering at the same time. Creeping chilliness : in single parts : in places of pus formation, or ulceration. Worse at night. [ Top ] RHUS TOX. Erysipelas of the vesicular variety, accompanied by restlessness . Erysipelas of face with burning ; large blisters, rapidly extending : becomes very purple and pits on pressure. Often extends from left to right across face. Rhus is worse from damp : from cold : relieved, temporarily, by motion. [ Top ] SECALE CORNUTUM Gangrenous erysipelas : competes with Ars. The only distinguishing feature between the two remedies may be that Secale wants cold and Arsenicum wants heat. Burning : "sparks of fire" falling on the part. Formication : "mice creeping under the skin." [ Top ] THUJA dematous erysipelas of face. Cases that occur in the much vaccinated may need Thuja , or cases that occur after vaccination . A curious, characteristic symptom, profuse sweat only on uncovered parts. [ Top ] VERATRUM VIRIDE "One peculiar symptom I have verified in a very severe case of erysipelas, which was accompanied by great delirium, is a narrow, well-defined red streak right through the middle of the tongue ." (NASH). "Phlegmonous erysipelas of face and head." (CLARKE). LESS SEVERE CASES. [ Top ] AMMONIUM CARB. "Erysipelas of old, debilitated persons. Eruption faintly developed, or has seemed to disappear, from weakness of patient's vitality to keep it on the surface. With cerebral symptoms, simulating a drunken stupor" (NASH). "Eruption comes out, and does not give relief to the patient." "Erysipelas of old people when cerebral symptoms are developed." Defective reaction. [ Top ] ARNICA "Erysipelas of face, with soreness , and sore bruised feeling all over the body : you need not wait longer before prescribing Arnica ." "Bed feels too hard : must move to get into a new place." " Rhus moves from restlessness and uneasiness, cannot lie still : Arnica , to ease the soreness by getting into a new place" (KENT). [ Top ] GRAPHITES "Eruptions oozing out a thick, honey-like fluid... Erysipelas sometimes takes this form, and in such cases recurs again and again." ( Sulph. ) Erysipelatous, moist, scrufy sores. Or, "Thin, sticky , glutinous, transparent watery fluid" (GUERNSEY, Keynotes ). [ Top ] HEPAR Any trouble occurring on the skin, when there is great sensitiveness to the slightest touch ( Canth. ). Extreme sensitiveness runs through the whole remedy : to the slightest draught of air : to the slightest noise : and also mental sensitiveness and irritability - almost to murder, when angered. [ Top ] PULSATILLA Erysipelas in the typical Pulsatilla patient . Mild, but irritable : changeable : weeps : craves sympathy. Craves open air : cool air : worse for heat. Not hungry or thirsty. [ Top ] SULPHUR Recurrent attacks of erysipelas ( Graph. ). Much burning : worse from heat of bed or room. Purplish appearance ( Lach. ). "For erysipelas, as a name, we have no remedy, but when a patient has erysipelas and his symptoms conform to those of Sulphur , you will cure him with Sulph ." (KENT). "When symptoms agree, Sulph. will be found a curative medicine in erysipelas." The typical Sulph. patient is hungry, especially at 10 to 11 A. M. Loves fat, "Eats anything." Kicks off the clothes at night, or puts feet out ; Craves, or hates, or is worse from fats. His eruptions itch ; are worse from heat, warm room, warm bed and from washing. Worse at night. Skin cannot bear woollens. The untidy ragged philosopher. Selfish. " Sulphur may be given on a paucity of symptoms." [ Top ] >>>>> Copyright © Médi-T 2003

sections.title: Eyes
sections.text: POINTERS TO THE COMMON REMEDIES. by Margaret Lucy Tyler Presented by Médi-T. Main * A * B * C * D * E * F * G * H * I * K * L * M * N * O * P * R * S * T * U * V * W * Z SOME COMMON EYE REMEDIES WITH INDICATIONS. Aco. * Apis * Arg. n. * Arn. * Ars. * Bell. * Cham. * Cina * Con. * Euphr. * Euphr. 2 * Graph. * Kali bi. * Lach. * Led. * Luet. * Med. * Merc. * Merc. cor. * Merc. cy. * Phos. * Puls. * Rhus * Ruta * Sant. * Staph. * Sulph. * Symph. [ Top ] ACONITE "For acute ophthalmia the first remedy is Aconite ; after which a dose of Bell. is generally sufficient to cure the disease." (Lilienthal.) First stage, prior to exudation. Excessive painfulness of eye, it feels dry and burning, great sensitiveness to air, and motion of balls. Photophobia. Aconite is anxious and restless. [ Top ] BELLADONNA "Glistening eyes : dilated pupils : flushed face. Intense redness of the inflamed part." "Inflammation of all the tissues of eyes, the lids and all parts of the eyeball, with most violent pain." HEAT : REDNESS : BURNING. "Pulsation, tumefaction, lachrymation : in tense pain : all worse from motion and light." Eye congested and red. Strange freaks in the field of vision-flickerings, flashes, sparks, double vision. Craving for lemons : lemon juice. Dilated pupils : contracted pupils. Inflammation of optic nerve and retina. [ Top ] CHAMOMILLA "High grade inflammation of eyes with bleeding. Oozing of bloody water from the newly born infant. Cham . will cure if there is some irritability of temper." Acrid discharges : purulent discharges. Intense photophobia. Violent pressure in orbital region ; eyes feel tightly compressed from all sides. Inflammation from damp cold, from every change to cold weather. Face (typically) red and hot on one side, the other pale. Cham . is worse 9 A. M. and 9 P. M. Intensely sensitive : irritable : restless : Driven frantic by pain. Capriciousness. [ Top ] PHOSPHORUS Eyes red, burn, smart : better for cold applications ( Apis : rev. of Ars .). Photophobia. Congestion and enlargement of blood vessels. Incipient cataract : sees better in twilight. Has cured glaucoma, retinitis in Bright's disease, opacity of vitreous. But in a Phos . patient-the artistic type, tall, slender ; desire for cold drinks, for salt : nervous. Letters may look red when reading ; (Yellow vision, Santonin : things look black, Stram .) [ Top ] CONIUM "Photophobia intense, out of all proportion to the objective signs of inflammation in the eye. Pains are worse at night, and terribly aggravated by least ray of light. > in dark room, and by pressure." (Nash.) ? ulcers on cornea. Falling of eyelids. ( Gels ., Caust ., Sep .) A characteristic of Conium , Sweats, day or night, as soon as one sleeps, or even closing the eyes. [ Top ] SULPHUR "Complaints of the eyes in a Sulphur patient." Eye symptoms made worse by washing.
